key_insight: A single multimodal agent can orchestrate and chain specialized AIGC components into end-to-end workflows, enabling complex multimedia content generation and editing across video, audio, image, and text modalities.
problem_solved: Current AIGC models are siloed — each handles a specific modality or subtask — forcing experts to manually stitch components into pipelines. The paper addresses the lack of a unified agent that understands intent, decomposes tasks, and coordinates multimodal generation and iterative editing.
method: Modular agent architecture that integrates modality-specific generators (video, audio, image, text) with a central planner and controller to coordinate sub-tasks.
Intent understanding and task decomposition: translate user goals into ordered subtasks and choose appropriate models/prompts for each modality.
Iterative refinement loop with grounding/context retrieval and editing primitives so outputs can be evaluated and updated until they meet user requirements.
impact: Makes multimedia AIGC practical for real-world production by reducing integration overhead and enabling end-to-end automated pipelines — speeding prototyping and improving consistency in cross-modal content creation.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram showing the agent at center orchestrating multiple modality-specific models (text, image, audio, video) and a planner/controller.
Before/after media examples (e.g., raw footage → scripted edits → final rendered video) to illustrate end-to-end capability.
Flowchart of task decomposition: user intent → subtasks → model selection → iterative feedback loop.
Bar chart or schematic comparing a multi-component manual workflow vs. the unified agent (time, steps, error points).
paper_title: A Versatile Multimodal Agent for Multimedia Content Generation
paper_authors: Daoan Zhang, Wenlin Yao, Xiaoyang Wang, Yebowen Hu, Jiebo Luo
